headline: No meaningful interaction risk: both open-source docs-only agents are non-runnable with no shared I/O, writes, or network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. Agent A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; agent B has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, MCP, or browser surfaces. With no shared channel, B cannot ingest A’s outputs by default.
conditions: IF either agent is wrapped in an external orchestrator that copies outputs between them, reassess injection risk.
IF a shared clipboard, file drop, or MCP bridge is added, the pathway becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from any shared clipboard or message bus.
Do not add an MCP bridge between the agents.
Require manual copy-paste only if outputs must be transferred.
Document that agent A is non-runnable and cannot emit tool outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is evident. Agent A touches no data classes and has network egress none; agent B also has no filesystem read, no API calls, and no network egress. Without shared storage or outbound transport, neither agent can leak the other’s data.
conditions: IF either agent is given a shared workspace or mounted files, leakage risk should be re-evaluated.
IF outbound network access is enabled for either agent, data exfiltration becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate, empty workspaces.
Leave network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid mounting sensitive files into either runtime.
Verify no API-calling surface is enabled on agent B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no write-conflict pathway. Agent A exposes no write or shell capabilities and is non-runnable; agent B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable surface, concurrent conflict is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk should be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state, the pathway may open.
mitigations: Keep agent B read-only as configured.
Do not grant agent A any runtime or write surface.
Avoid shared git repositories or writable mounts.
Use separate process sandboxes for any future execution.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not plausible here. Agent A is a static awesome-list and non-runnable; agent B is documentation-only and has no action-taking or API surfaces. Since B cannot act on A’s output, there is no downstream automation to cascade.
conditions: IF agent B is connected to an external executor that treats A’s text as authoritative, reassess.
IF either agent is upgraded to produce executable actions, cascading risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep agent B in documentation-only mode.
Do not wire A’s outputs into any action executor.
Require human review before any downstream action.
Add a validation step if future automation is introduced.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes; neither lists regulated data handling, residency constraints, or retention policies. With no sensitive data flow, there is no documented compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF either agent begins handling regulated data classes, compliance should be re-evaluated.
IF residency, retention, or certification requirements are introduced, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document that neither agent handles secrets or PHI.
Review any future retention policy before deployment.
Avoid cross-border data routing for this pair.
